title: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.uncurry_poincareMap
statement: Let l be a prime and k a field of characteristic p>0 with p != l. Let X, S be separated schemes of finite type over Spec k (objects of Over (Spec k)) and p:X\to S a morphism over k whose underlying morphism of schemes is smooth of pure relative dimension d (d in N). Write Qlb for the condensed ring Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj l and D^b_c(T)[[Qlb]] for the bounded constructible derived category of Qlb-module objects on the pro-etale site of T, a monoidal closed full subcategory of the ambient derived category (isMonoidal_boundedConstructible, isMonoidalClosed_boundedConstructible), with unit Qlb_T and internal hom RHom. On it Lp^* -| Rp_* (boundedConstructibleUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction) and Rp_! -| Rp^! (boundedConstructibleUpperShriekAdjunction, Rp^! = boundedConstructibleUpperShriek built from a Nagata compactification), and PF^!: Rp_! K (x) B \to Rp_!(K (x) Lp^* B) is the derived exceptional projection morphism (boundedConstructibleExceptionalProjection). Qlb_X(d)[2d] = boundedConstructibleTateTwist l X d (2d) is the shift by 2d of the Tate twist tateTwistDerived X l d [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists], bounded constructible by [nt-target-poincare-tate-bc], and pur_p: Rp^! Qlb_S ~= Qlb_X(d)[2d] (boundedConstructibleSmoothPurityIso) is the preimage under the fully faithful inclusion D^b_c \to D of the chosen smooth purity isomorphism smoothPurityIso l p d [nt-target-smooth-purity-qbar]. The Poincare duality morphism PD_p: Rp_* Qlb_X(d)[2d] \to RHom(Rp_! Qlb_X, Qlb_S) (poincareMap) is the composite of Rp_*(pur_p^{-1}), Rp_* of the identification Rp^! Qlb_S \to RHom(Qlb_X, Rp^! Qlb_S) (transpose of the left unitor) and the Verdier exchange morphism Phi_{p,K,L}: Rp_* RHom(K, Rp^! L) \to RHom(Rp_! K, L) at K=Qlb_X, L=Qlb_S, where Phi is the transpose of the pairing Rp_! K (x) Rp_* RHom(K,Rp^! L) \to Rp_!(K (x) Lp^* Rp_* RHom(K,Rp^! L)) \to Rp_!(K (x) RHom(K,Rp^! L)) \to Rp_! Rp^! L \to L (PF^!, the counit of Lp^* -| Rp_*, evaluation, the counit of Rp_! -| Rp^!). The trace Tr_p: Rp_! Qlb_X(d)[2d] \to Qlb_S (trace) is Rp_!(pur_p^{-1}) followed by the counit of Rp_! -| Rp^!, and the compact-support cup product cup_c: Rp_! Qlb_X (x) Rp_* Qlb_X(d)[2d] \to Rp_! Qlb_X(d)[2d] (cupProduct) is PF^!, Rp_!(Qlb_X (x) counit of Lp^* -| Rp_*) and the left unitor. Then the transpose uncurry(PD_p): Rp_! Qlb_X (x) Rp_* Qlb_X(d)[2d] \to Qlb_S of PD_p equals cup_c followed by Tr_p (Poincare duality is the trace-cup pairing). Upstream proves it as an instance of the sorry-free abstract identity CategoryTheory.Verdier.uncurry_poincareMap of WeilConjectures.PoincareDuality.Abstract.

proof.text:
Put $F=Rp_!$, $R=Rp^!$, $U=Lp^*$, $V=Rp_*$, $A=\mathbf1_X$, $B=\mathbf1_S$, $T=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}(d)[2d]$, $D=RB$, and $\theta=\mathrm{pur}_p^{-1}:T\to D$. Write $\epsilon:UV\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\delta:FR\to\mathrm{id}$ for the two counits, $\pi_{K,Z}:FK\otimes Z\to F(K\otimes UZ)$ for the projection transformation, and $\lambda_D:A\otimes D\to D$ for the left unitor. Let $j=\operatorname{curry}(\lambda_D):D\to[A,D]$ and $h=\theta;j$. These are exactly the maps in the target's definition, so $\mathrm{PD}_p=Vh;\Phi_{A,B}$. By the first two laws of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] (precomposition with $Vh$, then cancellation of $\Phi=\operatorname{curry}$ of the pairing) and the definition of $\Phi$ as a transpose,
$$\operatorname{uncurry}(\mathrm{PD}_p)=(1_{FA}\otimes Vh);\pi_{A,V[A,D]};F(1_A\otimes\epsilon_{[A,D]});F(\mathrm{ev}_{A,D});\delta_B.$$
All terms are in the bounded constructible categories specified in the target; no comparison with ordinary étale coefficients or passage to a point category is used.

proof.text:
Naturality of the projection transformation at $Vh:VT\to V[A,D]$ gives
$$(1_{FA}\otimes Vh);\pi_{A,V[A,D]}=\pi_{A,VT};F(1_A\otimes UVh).$$
Naturality of the adjunction counit at $h:T\to[A,D]$ gives $UVh;\epsilon_{[A,D]}=\epsilon_T;h$. Substitute both equations into step 1 and use preservation of composition by $F$ and by tensoring. The result is
$$\pi_{A,VT};F(1_A\otimes\epsilon_T);F(1_A\otimes h);F(\mathrm{ev}_{A,D});\delta_B.$$
These are the naturality equations in the definition of the two natural transformations, not a projection-formula isomorphism or a base-change theorem.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: the tensor–internal-Hom chain is the transpose of the cup/evaluation/normalized-trace composite.

proof.text:
The evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_{A,D}$ in the definition of $\Phi$ is the counit of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction at $D$. By the third law of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], $(1_A\otimes j);\mathrm{ev}_{A,D}=\operatorname{uncurry}(j)$, and since $j=\operatorname{curry}(\lambda_D)$ its first law gives $\operatorname{uncurry}(j)=\lambda_D$. Hence
$$(1_A\otimes h);\mathrm{ev}_{A,D}=(1_A\otimes\theta);\lambda_D=\lambda_T;\theta,$$
where the final equality is the naturality axiom of the left unitor from [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Substitution into step 2 and the functor composition law give
$$\operatorname{uncurry}(\mathrm{PD}_p)=\pi_{A,VT};F(1_A\otimes\epsilon_T);F(\lambda_T);F(\theta);\delta_B.$$
By the target's definitions the first three factors are $\mathrm{cup}_c$ and the last two are $\mathrm{Tr}_p$. This is the claimed equality. All expressions use two tensor factors in the displayed order; no omitted reassociation or symmetry changes the morphism.
